exposure: provision of cesarean sections as primary surgeon by family physicians
Provision of cesarean sections as primary surgeon
Practice location (rural health clinics, small rural counties, counties without obstetrician/gynecologists)
outcome: Provision of cesarean sections as primary surgeon by family physicians
cohort: 28,526 family physicians from the 2017-2022 American Board of Family Medicine's Continuing Certification Questionnaire
finding: Family physicians who provide cesarean sections as primary surgeons are more likely to be male and work in rural settings, particularly those without obstetrician/gynecologists, suggesting their importance in maintaining obstetric access in these underserved areas.
mod_finding: Family physicians who provide cesarean sections as primary surgeon disproportionately serve rural communities and counties without obstetrician/gynecologists, suggesting that they provide access to obstetric services in these communities.
